To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
reference genes for normalization of expression data during diurinal/circadian studies need to be chosen with extra care as the majority of the transcriptome undergoes cycling.

the reference genes for diurnal/ciradian studies should not be selected based on stability analysis only as more than 50% of transcriptome is rhythmic, and hence, a combination of two or more stable reference genes is recommended for diurnal studies.

the house-keeping (reference) genes should be selected with extra caution for diurnal/circa-dian studies in plants as more than 70% of transcriptome undergoes rhythmic expression, which is not detected by the gene stability software, thereby affecting the results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validation of house-keeping gene stability for normalization of RT-qPCR data for diurnal/cicardian studies in rice.
the validation of the house-keeping gene selection for diurnal/ciradian studies in plants and the findings are of great importance to the researchers working on the circadian clock in rice.
a comprehensive validation of house-keeping gene stability for normalization of RT-qPCR based expression data during diurnalcircadian studies in the rice plant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of reference genes for normalization of RT-qPCR data should be made with utmost care and the expression of the reference genes should be checked before using them for normalization.
, the use of house-keeping gene(s) as a reference for normalization of gene expressions in diurnal/circational studies is a risky proposition and should be avoided.

, although the use of multiple reference genes is the best option, the use of two or more reference genes is recommended for diurnal and circadian studies in plants, and that, if only one reference gene has to be used, the geometric mean of two most stable reference genes should be considered for normalization of RT-qPCR data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the choice of reference genes for RT-qPCR based expression profiling should be made with caution and should be validated with the samples under study.
the expression of genes that regulate the diurnal/circannual rhythms in plants should be normalized with the help of reference genes that do not undergo rhythmic expression.
the expression profiles of reference genes should always be validated before using them for normalization of gene of interest in RT-qPCR experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of house-keeping gene is not always stable and can be cyclic in nature.
the choice of house-keeping gene(s) is crucial and needs to be carefully validated before using them for gene expression studies.
the house-keeping gene selection is a crucial step for the reliability of the results of RT-qPCR based diurnal/circational gene expression studies.
